decisions.choice: the word that came to Jeremiah: a heading that opens a new message
decisions.reason: The same heading opens the temple sermon in 7:1 and other messages (18:1; 21:1). What follows is a sermon in prose about the covenant, running to verse 17; verses 18-23 then turn to a plot against Jeremiah's life.

decisions.choice: a message given at a time the text does not state
decisions.reason: The sermon is not dated. Its call to hear "the words of this covenant" echoes the covenant King Josiah renewed after the book of the law was found in the temple (2 Kings 23:2-3), so it may come from his reign, but the chapter itself does not say so.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying: / ...: / This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah:
decisions.reason: The book's fixed wording for this heading (as in 7:1). Balanced drops "saying", which only introduces the quotation, and Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: the words of this covenant: the covenant God made with Israel at Sinai and renewed in Moab, as Deuteronomy sets it out
decisions.reason: "The words of this covenant" is Deuteronomy's phrase for the covenant terms Moses set before Israel (Deuteronomy 28:69; 29:8). It is also the phrase used when Josiah renewed the covenant (2 Kings 23:3). The whole sermon is built from Deuteronomy's language.

decisions.choice: hear (spoken to more than one) ... speak them (spoken to one): the call to hear is general, the task of speaking is Jeremiah's
alternatives: both commands are to Jeremiah alone
decisions.reason: The first verb is plural and the second singular. The plural may call on everyone, or on Jeremiah with others, to hear the covenant; the singular gives Jeremiah the task of passing it on. Verse 6 has a similar pair.

decisions.choice: man of Judah: the people of Judah as a whole
decisions.reason: The singular noun "man" with a place name is a collective way of naming the people of a land (2 Kings 23:2). The covenant was given to all the people (Deuteronomy 29:9-10).

decisions.choice: the people of Judah, with "the men of Judah" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew collective means the whole people, so the inclusive form is the default; the traditional wording is the alternative. Readable says "the people", which needs no alternative.

decisions.choice: "Oigan"/"Escuchen" (plural); "háblalas", "comunícalas" (singular)
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew, the call to hear is plural and takes the plural you setting, while the task of speaking is given to Jeremiah alone, "tú". "Pacto" for covenant, as published.

decisions.choice: "la gente de Judá", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "gente" covers men and women, so the English gender setting needs no Spanish span; Literal keeps "los hombres de Judá", as the English alternative does.

decisions.choice: Sikieni (plural) ... ukawaambie (singular)
decisions.reason: Swahili shows in the verbs what the English must leave unseen (meaning decision m2): the call to hear is to many, the charge to speak is to Jeremiah. "Watu wa Yuda" covers men and women, so the English gender span has no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: "aux gens de Juda", with "aux hommes de Juda" as the gender setting's alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew collective "man of Judah" means the whole people, so the inclusive word is the default, as in the English.

decisions.choice: cursed is the one who does not obey: the closing curse of the covenant ceremony
decisions.reason: The words echo the last of the curses the Levites were to pronounce at Mount Ebal, "Cursed is the one who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them", to which all the people answered "Amen" (Deuteronomy 27:26). Jeremiah's "Amen" in verse 5 completes the echo.

decisions.choice: hear: listen and obey
decisions.reason: The verb "hear" with words or a voice as its object often means to obey them (Deuteronomy 28:15). Hearing without doing is not hearing at all in this sermon (verse 8).

decisions.choice: cursed: under God's sentence of harm
decisions.reason: A curse in the covenant is not a magic spell but the harm God declares will fall on those who break it (Deuteronomy 28:15-68).

decisions.choice: the one, with "the man" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: "The man" here means any person, so Literal uses the inclusive form by default. Balanced and Readable say "anyone".

decisions.choice: A curse will fall on anyone ... (a full sentence)
decisions.reason: Readable ends the sentence here and starts a new one in verse 4, where Literal and Balanced continue with a comma.

decisions.choice: the iron furnace: Egypt as a place of fierce suffering from which God took Israel
decisions.reason: Moses used the same picture: God took Israel "out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt" to be his own people (Deuteronomy 4:20; also 1 Kings 8:51). A furnace for smelting iron burns hotter than any other, so the picture is of the harshest affliction.

decisions.choice: you will be my people, and I will be your God: the heart of the covenant
decisions.reason: This pair of promises sums up the covenant from the exodus on (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). Jeremiah repeats it in his temple sermon (7:23) and in the promise of a new covenant (31:33).

decisions.choice: do them: carry out the words of the covenant
decisions.reason: "Them" refers back to "the words of this covenant" in verse 3.

decisions.choice: fathers: ancestors, the generation of the exodus
decisions.reason: The word "fathers" here means the forebears of the nation, those God brought out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", since the word means the forebears of the nation (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Egypt had been like a blazing furnace for them
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the furnace is a picture of Egypt and what Israel suffered there.

alternatives: three levels of the same marks
decisions.reason: French nests « », “ ” and ‘ ’, as the English nests its double and single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the oath ... a land flowing with milk and honey: God's sworn promise to the patriarchs
decisions.reason: God swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to give their descendants the land (Deuteronomy 7:8; 8:18), described as flowing with milk and honey, a picture of rich pasture and plenty (Exodus 3:8).

decisions.choice: as this day: as is the case now
decisions.reason: The phrase points to the present: the promise has been kept, and the people live in the land (Deuteronomy 8:18). Breaking the covenant now would be ingratitude for a promise fulfilled.

decisions.choice: amen: it is true, so let it be
decisions.reason: "Amen" is the answer the people gave to each covenant curse (Deuteronomy 27:15-26). Jeremiah answers as the whole people should have done, accepting the covenant and its curse.

decisions.choice: and I answered: Jeremiah's reply ends God's words
decisions.reason: The words God told Jeremiah to say end with "as this day"; Jeremiah then speaks in his own voice. So the quotations close before his answer.

decisions.choice: Let it be so
decisions.reason: Readable adds what "Amen" means for a reader who may know it only as the end of a prayer (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Amen, LORD (no "O")
decisions.reason: The divine name addressed directly is written without "O", as in the Psalms and Isaiah.

decisions.choice: Amina, Ee BWANA
decisions.reason: Swahili addresses God with "Ee", as the published Psalms, where the English leaves out "O".

decisions.choice: "un pays où coulent le lait et le miel"

decisions.reason: The settled French wording of the Pentateuch for this phrase.

decisions.choice: proclaim: call out in public
decisions.reason: The verb means to call aloud. Jeremiah is to announce the covenant in the open, where everyone can hear, in every town and street.

decisions.choice: saying: the public message runs through verse 8
decisions.reason: What Jeremiah is to proclaim begins with the call to hear and do the covenant and continues with God's account of the ancestors in verses 7-8, spoken to the people ("your fathers").

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The towns of Judah were mostly small walled settlements, so Balanced and Readable say "towns". Literal keeps "cities".

records.literal_gloss: For warning solemnly I warned your fathers in [the] day of my bringing up them from [the] land of Egypt and until the day the this, rising early and warning, saying, Listen to my voice.

en.L: For I solemnly warned your fathers on the day I brought them up from the land of Egypt, and until this day, rising early and warning, saying, "Listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice."
en.B: For I warned your ancestors in the strongest terms when I brought them up from the land of Egypt, and I have warned them again and again until today: "Listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice."
en.R: I warned your ancestors very seriously when I brought them out of Egypt. And I have kept warning your people over and over until now. I told them, "Obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Porque advertí solemnemente a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}} el día en que los hice subir de la tierra de Egipto, y hasta este día, madrugando y advirtiendo, diciendo: ‘{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz’.
es.B: Porque advertí con toda seriedad a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} cuando los hice subir de la tierra de Egipto, y los he advertido una y otra vez hasta hoy: ‘{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz’.
es.R: Advertí muy seriamente a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} cuando los saqué de Egipto. Y he seguido advirtiendo a {{plural_you:su pueblo|vuestro pueblo}} una y otra vez hasta ahora. Les dije: ‘{{plural_you:Obedézcanme|Obedecedme}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}’.

fr.L: Car j’ai averti solennellement vos pères le jour où je les ai fait monter du pays d’Égypte, et jusqu’à ce jour, me levant de bonne heure et avertissant, en disant : ‘Écoutez {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix.’
fr.B: Car j’ai averti vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} avec la plus grande force quand je les ai fait monter du pays d’Égypte, et je les ai avertis sans relâche jusqu’à aujourd’hui : ‘Écoutez {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix.’
fr.R: J’ai averti très sérieusement vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} quand je les ai fait sortir d’Égypte. Et j’ai continué à avertir votre peuple encore et encore jusqu’à maintenant. Je leur ai dit : ‘Obéissez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.’

sw.L: Kwa maana niliwaonya baba zenu kwa dhati siku ile nilipowapandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri, hata siku hii ya leo, nikiamka mapema na kuonya, nikisema, "Isikilizeni sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}."
sw.B: Kwa maana niliwaonya babu zenu kwa maneno makali kabisa nilipowapandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri, nami nimewaonya tena na tena mpaka leo: "Isikilizeni sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}."
sw.R: Niliwaonya babu zenu kwa uzito mkubwa nilipowatoa Misri. Nami nimeendelea kuwaonya watu wenu mara nyingi sana mpaka sasa. Niliwaambia, "Nitiini."

decisions.choice: warning I warned: an earnest, solemn warning
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. It means to warn as a witness does, calling someone to account (Deuteronomy 8:19; 30:19).

decisions.choice: rising early and warning: warning persistently, without letting up
decisions.reason: Rising early to do something means doing it with urgency and doing it again and again. Jeremiah uses the phrase often of God sending his prophets (7:13, 25; 25:3-4).

decisions.choice: verses 7-8 are read as the Hebrew text has them
alternatives: the shorter text of the Greek translation
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation does not have most of verses 7-8; it moves from verse 6 to the words "but they did not do [them]" at the end of verse 8. The Greek of Jeremiah is shorter than the Hebrew throughout the book (see the note at 1:1).

decisions.choice: rising early and warning / again and again / over and over
decisions.reason: The book's fixed wording for this phrase: Literal keeps the picture, Balanced and Readable give its sense (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: kept warning your people
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the warnings went on through the generations after the exodus, down to the people Jeremiah addresses.

en.L: But they did not listen, and they did not incline their ear, and they walked, each one, in the stubbornness of their evil heart. So I brought on them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded [them] to do, but they did not do [them].'"

fr.L: Mais ils n’ont pas écouté, et ils n’ont pas tendu l’oreille, et ils ont marché, chacun, selon l’obstination de leur cœur mauvais. Alors j’ai fait venir sur eux toutes les paroles de cette alliance, que je [leur] avais ordonné de pratiquer, mais qu’ils n’ont pas pratiquées.” »
fr.B: Mais ils n’ont pas écouté ni prêté attention. Chacun a suivi l’obstination de son cœur mauvais. Alors j’ai fait venir sur eux tout ce dont cette alliance les menaçait, car je leur avais ordonné de l’observer, et ils ne l’ont pas observée.” »
fr.R: Mais ils n’ont pas écouté et n’ont pas fait attention. Chacun a suivi avec obstination son propre cœur mauvais. Alors j’ai fait venir sur eux toutes les punitions dont cette alliance les avertissait. Je leur avais ordonné de lui obéir, mais ils ne l’ont pas fait.” »

sw.B: Lakini hawakusikiliza wala hawakujali. Kila mmoja wao alikwenda katika ukaidi wa moyo wake mwovu. Kwa hiyo nikaleta juu yao yote ambayo agano hili linaonya, kwa maana niliwaamuru kulishika, lakini hawakulishika.'"
sw.R: Lakini hawakusikiliza wala hawakujali. Kila mmoja wao alifuata kwa ukaidi moyo wake mwovu. Kwa hiyo nikaleta juu yao adhabu zote ambazo agano hili linaonya juu yake. Niliwaamuru kulitii, lakini hawakulitii.'"

decisions.choice: incline the ear: turn to listen, pay attention
decisions.reason: To bend the ear toward someone is to listen with care. The phrase recurs in Jeremiah's sermons (7:24, 26; 17:23).

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of their evil heart: hard, self-willed refusal
decisions.reason: The rare noun means firmness or hardness. Deuteronomy uses it of a person who walks "in the stubbornness of my heart" and still expects peace (Deuteronomy 29:18); Jeremiah uses it eight times.

decisions.choice: all the words of this covenant: here, the curses it threatens
decisions.reason: The covenant's words include its curses on those who break it (Deuteronomy 28:15; 29:19-20). God carried out what he had warned; the same "words" that called them to obey now fall on them as judgment.

decisions.choice: all that this covenant threatens / all the punishments this covenant warns about
alternatives: all the words of this covenant
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the covenant's "words" are in this sentence (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "words".

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of their evil heart / hearts / stubbornly followed their own evil hearts
decisions.reason: The book's fixed wording for this phrase.

decisions.choice: conspiracy: a plot of disloyalty, treason
decisions.reason: The word is used for plots against a king (2 Kings 11:14; 15:30). Here the treason is against God, the covenant's King: verse 10 says what it is, a turning back to other gods.

decisions.choice: has been found: has been discovered, exposed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of wrongdoers caught in the act (Exodus 22:1). What the people did together in secret has been found out by God.

decisions.choice: man of Judah: the people of Judah as a whole
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: I have uncovered
decisions.reason: Readable turns the passive verb into an active one with God, the speaker, as the one who uncovered the plot.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah, with "the men of Judah" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

source.text: שָׁ֩בוּ֩ עַל־עֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתָ֜ם הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר מֵֽאֲנוּ֙ לִשְׁמ֣וֹעַ אֶת־דְּבָרַ֔י וְהֵ֣מָּה הָלְכ֗וּ אַחֲרֵ֛י אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים לְעָבְדָ֑ם הֵפֵ֤רוּ בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֕י אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖תִּי אֶת־אֲבוֹתָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They have turned back to [the] iniquities of their fathers the first, who refused to hear my words, and they have gone after gods other to serve them; they have broken, [the] house of Israel and [the] house of Judah, my covenant which I cut with their fathers.

en.L: They have turned back to the iniquities of their first fathers, who refused to hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, and they have gone after other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, which I made with their fathers.
en.B: They have gone back to the sins of their earliest ancestors, who refused to listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words; they too have followed other gods and served them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have both broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, the one I made with their ancestors.
en.R: They have gone back to the sins of their ancestors long ago, who refused to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They have followed other gods and worshiped them. The people of Israel and the people of Judah have both broken the covenant I made with their ancestors.

es.L: Se han vuelto a las iniquidades de sus primeros padres, que rehusaron oír {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras, y se han ido tras otros dioses para servirlos. La casa de Israel y la casa de Judá han quebrantado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto, el que hice con sus padres.
es.B: Han vuelto a los pecados de sus primeros antepasados, que se negaron a escuchar {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras; también ellos han seguido a otros dioses y los han servido. La casa de Israel y la casa de Judá han quebrantado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto, el que hice con sus antepasados.
es.R: Han vuelto a los pecados de sus antepasados de hace mucho tiempo, que se negaron a escuchar{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Han seguido a otros dioses y los han adorado. El pueblo de Israel y el pueblo de Judá han quebrantado el pacto que hice con sus antepasados.

fr.L: Ils sont retournés aux fautes de leurs premiers pères, qui ont refusé d’écouter {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, et ils sont allés derrière d’autres dieux pour les servir. La maison d’Israël et la maison de Juda ont rompu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} alliance, que j’avais conclue avec leurs pères.
fr.B: Ils sont revenus aux péchés de leurs plus anciens {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, qui ont refusé d’écouter {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles ; eux aussi ont suivi d’autres dieux et les ont servis. La maison d’Israël et la maison de Juda ont toutes deux rompu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} alliance, celle que j’avais conclue avec leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}.
fr.R: Ils sont revenus aux péchés de leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} d’autrefois, qui ont refusé de {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écouter. Ils ont suivi d’autres dieux et les ont adorés. Le peuple d’Israël et le peuple de Juda ont tous deux rompu l’alliance que j’avais conclue avec leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}.

sw.L: Wamerudia maovu ya baba zao wa kwanza, waliokataa kusikia maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nao wamefuata miungu mingine kuitumikia. Nyumba ya Israeli na nyumba ya Yuda wamelivunja agano {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} nililofanya na baba zao.
sw.B: Wamerudi kwenye dhambi za babu zao wa kwanza kabisa, waliokataa kuyasikiliza maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; nao pia wamefuata miungu mingine na kuitumikia. Nyumba ya Israeli na nyumba ya Yuda wote wamelivunja agano {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, lile nililofanya na babu zao.
sw.R: Wamerudi kwenye dhambi za babu zao wa zamani, waliokataa kunisikiliza. Wamefuata miungu mingine na kuiabudu. Watu wa Israeli na watu wa Yuda wote wamevunja agano nililofanya na babu zao.

decisions.choice: their first fathers: the earliest generations, from the exodus on
alternatives: the ancestors of the generation just before
decisions.reason: "The first" points back to the generation God brought out of Egypt (verses 4 and 7), who rebelled in the wilderness (Numbers 14:22-23), and the generations after them. The present generation has gone back to the very sins of the beginning.

decisions.choice: gone after other gods: followed them as a servant follows a master
decisions.reason: To walk after someone is to be their follower. This is the sin the covenant warned against above all (Deuteronomy 6:14; 8:19).

decisions.choice: the house of Israel and the house of Judah: both kingdoms of God's people
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom, Israel, had already been taken into exile by Assyria for this same sin (2 Kings 17:7-23). Judah, the southern kingdom, is now just as guilty.

decisions.choice: made a covenant: literally, cut a covenant
decisions.reason: Covenants were sealed by a sacrifice in which animals were cut (Genesis 15:9-18; Jeremiah 34:18), so the usual verb for making one is "cut".

decisions.choice: sins
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Balanced and Readable say "sins" where Literal keeps "iniquities".

decisions.choice: worshiped ... listen to me
decisions.reason: Readable says "worshiped" for serving gods, and "listen to me" for listening to God's words.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא אֲלֵיהֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יוּכְל֖וּ לָצֵ֣את מִמֶּ֑נָּה וְזָעֲק֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: behold I [am] bringing on them disaster which not they will be able to go out from it; and they will cry to me, and not I will listen to them.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am bringing on them disaster from which they will not be able to go out; and they will cry out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but I will not listen to them.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to bring a disaster on them that they will not be able to escape. When they cry out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will not listen to them.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to bring a disaster on them, and they will not be able to escape it. They will cry to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for help, but I will not listen to them.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: He aquí que traigo sobre ellos una desgracia de la que no podrán salir; y clamarán a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, pero no los escucharé.
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Voy a traer sobre ellos una desgracia de la que no podrán escapar. Cuando clamen a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no los escucharé.
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Voy a traer una desgracia sobre ellos, y no podrán escapar de ella. Ellos {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pedirán ayuda a gritos, pero no los escucharé.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Voici, je fais venir sur eux un malheur dont ils ne pourront pas sortir ; et ils crieront vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, mais je ne les écouterai pas.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je vais faire venir sur eux un malheur auquel ils ne pourront pas échapper. Quand ils crieront vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je ne les écouterai pas.
fr.R: Alors voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je vais faire venir sur eux un malheur, et ils ne pourront pas y échapper. Ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appelleront au secours, mais je ne les écouterai pas.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Tazama, ninaleta juu yao mabaya ambayo hawataweza kutoka ndani yake; nao watanililia, lakini sitawasikiliza.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Karibu nitaleta juu yao maafa ambayo hawataweza kuyaepuka. Watakaponililia, sitawasikiliza.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Nitaleta maafa juu yao, wala hawataweza kuyaepuka. Watanililia niwasaidie, lakini sitawasikiliza.

decisions.choice: disaster: harm and ruin, not moral evil
decisions.reason: The word can mean evil or disaster. Here it is what God brings on the people as judgment, as in verse 17 and 23.

decisions.choice: behold I am bringing: an action about to happen
decisions.reason: "Behold" with a participle announces something that is on the point of happening.

decisions.choice: they will cry to me, but I will not listen: the people's refusal to listen is answered in kind
decisions.reason: They would not listen to God (verses 8 and 10); now God will not listen to them. Deuteronomy warned that God would hide his face when they turned to other gods (Deuteronomy 31:17-18; also Micah 3:4).

decisions.choice: Look
decisions.reason: "Behold" is no longer used in modern English, so Literal says "Look". Balanced and Readable carry the sense with "I am about to" and "I am going to".

source.text: וְהָֽלְכ֞וּ עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וְיֹשְׁבֵי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְזָֽעֲקוּ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם מְקַטְּרִ֖ים לָהֶ֑ם וְהוֹשֵׁ֛עַ לֹֽא־יוֹשִׁ֥יעוּ לָהֶ֖ם בְּעֵ֥ת רָעָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will go [the] cities of Judah and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem and cry to the gods which they [are] making smoke to them, but saving not they will save them in [the] time of their disaster.

en.L: Then the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they make offerings smoke, but they will surely not save them in the time of their disaster.
en.B: Then the towns of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods they burn offerings to, but those gods will never save them when their disaster comes.
en.R: Then the people in the towns of Judah and in Jerusalem will go and pray to the gods they offer sacrifices to. But those gods will never be able to save them when disaster comes.

es.L: Entonces las ciudades de Judá y los habitantes de Jerusalén irán y clamarán a los dioses a los que queman ofrendas, pero ciertamente no los salvarán en el tiempo de su desgracia.
es.B: Entonces las ciudades de Judá y los que viven en Jerusalén irán a clamar a los dioses a los que queman ofrendas, pero esos dioses nunca los salvarán cuando llegue su desgracia.
es.R: Entonces la gente de los pueblos de Judá y de Jerusalén irá a orar a los dioses a los que ofrecen sacrificios. Pero esos dioses nunca podrán salvarlos cuando llegue la desgracia.

fr.L: Alors les villes de Juda et les habitants de Jérusalem iront crier vers les dieux auxquels ils font fumer des offrandes, mais ceux-ci ne les sauveront certainement pas au temps de leur malheur.
fr.B: Alors les villes de Juda et les habitants de Jérusalem iront crier vers les dieux auxquels ils brûlent des offrandes, mais ces dieux ne les sauveront jamais quand le malheur viendra.
fr.R: Alors les gens des villes de Juda et de Jérusalem iront prier les dieux auxquels ils offrent des sacrifices. Mais ces dieux ne pourront jamais les sauver quand le malheur arrivera.

sw.L: Ndipo miji ya Yuda na wakaaji wa Yerusalemu watakwenda na kuililia miungu ambayo wanaifukizia [sadaka], lakini hakika haitawaokoa wakati wa mabaya yao.
sw.B: Ndipo miji ya Yuda na wale wanaoishi Yerusalemu watakwenda na kuililia miungu wanayoifukizia sadaka, lakini miungu hiyo haitawaokoa kamwe maafa yao yatakapowajia.
sw.R: Ndipo watu wa miji ya Yuda na wa Yerusalemu watakwenda kuiomba miungu wanayoitolea dhabihu. Lakini miungu hiyo haitaweza kuwaokoa kamwe maafa yatakapokuja.

decisions.choice: make smoke: burn incense or offerings so that their smoke goes up
decisions.reason: The verb means to send up in smoke. It is used both of burning incense and of burning offerings to gods (2 Kings 23:5); either may be meant here.

decisions.choice: saving they will not save: they will not save them at all
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. The gods they served cannot help in the day of trouble (2:28; Deuteronomy 32:37-38; Judges 10:14).

decisions.choice: the people in the towns ... pray to
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people in the towns", since the towns stand for the people in them, and "pray" for crying out to a god.

decisions.choice: make offerings smoke / burn offerings / offer sacrifices
decisions.reason: The verb covers incense and offerings alike (meaning decision m1), so the renderings keep a general word rather than choosing incense.

source.text: כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר עָרֶ֔יךָ הָי֥וּ אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יְהוּדָ֑ה וּמִסְפַּ֞ר חֻצ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם שַׂמְתֶּ֤ם מִזְבְּחוֹת֙ לַבֹּ֔שֶׁת מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְקַטֵּ֥ר לַבָּֽעַל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For [the] number of your cities are your gods, Judah, and [the] number of [the] streets of Jerusalem you have set up altars to the shame, altars to make smoke to the Baal.

en.L: For [as many as] the number of your cities are your gods, Judah; and [as many as] the number of the streets of Jerusalem you have set up altars to the shameful thing, altars to make offerings smoke to Baal.
en.B: For you have as many gods as you have towns, Judah, and you have set up as many altars to that shameful thing as there are streets in Jerusalem, altars for burning offerings to Baal.
en.R: People of Judah, you have as many gods as you have towns! In Jerusalem you have built as many altars as there are streets. They are altars to that shameful god, altars for burning sacrifices to Baal.

es.L: Porque según el número de tus ciudades [son] tus dioses, Judá; y según el número de las calles de Jerusalén {{plural_you:han levantado|habéis levantado}} altares a la cosa vergonzosa, altares para quemar ofrendas a Baal.
es.B: Porque tienes tantos dioses como ciudades, Judá, y {{plural_you:han levantado|habéis levantado}} tantos altares a esa cosa vergonzosa como calles hay en Jerusalén, altares para quemar ofrendas a Baal.
es.R: ¡Gente de Judá, {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} tantos dioses como ciudades! En Jerusalén {{plural_you:han construido|habéis construido}} tantos altares como calles hay. Son altares a ese dios vergonzoso, altares para quemar sacrificios a Baal.

fr.L: Car autant tu as de villes, autant tu as de dieux, Juda ; et autant il y a de rues à Jérusalem, autant vous avez dressé d’autels à la honte, d’autels pour faire fumer des offrandes à Baal.
fr.B: Car tu as autant de dieux que de villes, Juda, et vous avez dressé à cette chose honteuse autant d’autels qu’il y a de rues à Jérusalem, des autels pour brûler des offrandes à Baal.
fr.R: Habitants de Juda, vous avez autant de dieux que de villes ! À Jérusalem, vous avez construit autant d’autels qu’il y a de rues. Ce sont des autels pour ce dieu honteux, des autels pour brûler des sacrifices à Baal.

sw.L: Kwa maana [kama] hesabu ya miji yako ndivyo ilivyo miungu yako, Yuda; na [kama] hesabu ya njia za Yerusalemu mmesimamisha madhabahu kwa kitu cha aibu, madhabahu za kumfukizia Baali [sadaka].
sw.B: Kwa maana una miungu mingi kama ulivyo na miji, ee Yuda, nanyi mmesimamisha madhabahu kwa kitu kile cha aibu nyingi kama zilivyo njia za Yerusalemu, madhabahu za kumfukizia Baali sadaka.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Yuda, mna miungu mingi kama mlivyo na miji! Katika Yerusalemu mmejenga madhabahu nyingi kama zilivyo njia. Ni madhabahu za mungu yule wa aibu, madhabahu za kumtolea Baali dhabihu.

decisions.choice: as many gods as cities: the same charge as in 2:28
decisions.reason: The first half of the verse repeats 2:28 word for word. Every town had its own god, so many that they could be counted by the towns.

decisions.choice: the shame: a scornful name for Baal
decisions.reason: "Shame" is used in place of Baal's name (3:24; Hosea 9:10). The same change was made in names: Saul's son Eshbaal (1 Chronicles 8:33) is called Ish-bosheth, "man of shame" (2 Samuel 2:8). Here the next words name Baal directly.

decisions.choice: Baal: the Canaanite storm god
decisions.reason: Baal was worshiped as the god who sent rain and gave fertility to the land. Israel was drawn to his worship again and again (Judges 2:11-13; 1 Kings 18).

decisions.choice: your (one) ... you have set up (many): Judah addressed as one and then as its people
decisions.reason: "Your cities" and "your gods" speak to Judah as a single person; "you have set up" turns to the people of Jerusalem as many.

decisions.choice: People of Judah ... that shameful god
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the people and says that "the shameful thing" is a god, which the end of the verse makes clear.

decisions.choice: "tus ciudades" (singular); "han levantado" in a plural_you span
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew, Judah is addressed first as one ("tú") and then as its people ("ustedes"). Readable speaks to the people throughout, as the English does.

decisions.choice: miji yako (singular) ... mmesimamisha (plural)
decisions.reason: Judah is addressed first as one and then as its people (meaning decision m4); Swahili shows the change in "yako" and the plural verb.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֗ה אַל־תִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ בְּעַד־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַל־תִּשָּׂ֥א בַעֲדָ֖ם רִנָּ֣ה וּתְפִלָּ֑ה כִּ֣י אֵינֶ֣נִּי שֹׁמֵ֗עַ בְּעֵ֛ת קָרְאָ֥ם אֵלַ֖י בְּעַ֥ד רָעָתָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, not pray for the people the this, and not lift up for them cry and prayer, for not I [am] listening in [the] time of their calling to me on account of their disaster.

en.L: As for you, do not pray for this people, and do not lift up a cry or a prayer for them, for I will not be listening when they call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} because of their disaster.
en.B: As for you, do not pray for this people. Do not lift up a cry or a prayer for them, because I will not listen when they call out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} because of their trouble.
en.R: But you, Jeremiah, must not pray for these people. Do not plead with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or pray for them. When disaster comes and they call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will not listen.

es.L: En cuanto a ti, no ores por este pueblo, ni eleves por ellos clamor ni oración, porque no escucharé cuando clamen a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} a causa de su desgracia.
es.B: En cuanto a ti, no ores por este pueblo. No eleves por ellos clamor ni oración, porque no escucharé cuando {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} llamen a causa de su aflicción.
es.R: Pero tú, Jeremías, no ores por esta gente. No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} supliques ni ores por ellos. Cuando llegue la desgracia y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} llamen, no escucharé.

fr.L: Et toi, ne prie pas pour ce peuple, et n’élève pour eux ni cri ni prière, car je n’écouterai pas quand ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appelleront à cause de leur malheur.
fr.B: Quant à toi, ne prie pas pour ce peuple. N’élève pour eux ni supplication ni prière, car je n’écouterai pas quand ils crieront vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} à cause de leur malheur.
fr.R: Mais toi, Jérémie, ne prie pas pour ce peuple. Ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} supplie pas et ne prie pas pour eux. Quand le malheur viendra et qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appelleront, je ne les écouterai pas.

sw.L: Nawe, usiwaombee watu hawa, wala usiwainulie kilio wala sala, kwa maana sitasikiliza wakati watakaponililia kwa sababu ya mabaya yao.
sw.B: Kwa upande wako, usiwaombee watu hawa. Usiinue kilio wala sala kwa ajili yao, kwa sababu sitasikiliza watakaponililia kwa sababu ya taabu yao.
sw.R: Lakini wewe, Yeremia, usiwaombee watu hawa. Usinisihi wala usiwaombee. Maafa yatakapokuja nao wakaniita, sitasikiliza.

decisions.choice: do not pray for this people: the prophet is forbidden to intercede
decisions.reason: Prophets prayed for the people, as Moses and Samuel did (Exodus 32:11-14; 1 Samuel 12:23). God's command not to pray (7:16; 14:11) shows that the judgment is now settled.

decisions.choice: cry: a loud, ringing cry, here a cry of pleading
decisions.reason: The word is often a shout of joy, but it is also a loud cry to God for help (1 Kings 8:28).

decisions.choice: because of their disaster
alternatives: in the time of their disaster
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads "on account of" their disaster. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "in the time of", as in verse 12, which differs by one letter. The sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed, the prophet.

source.text: מֶ֣ה לִֽידִידִ֞י בְּבֵיתִ֗י עֲשׂוֹתָ֤הּ הַֽמְזִמָּ֨תָה֙ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים וּבְשַׂר־קֹ֖דֶשׁ יַעַבְר֣וּ מֵֽעָלָ֑יִךְ כִּ֥י רָעָתֵ֖כִי אָ֥ז תַּעֲלֹֽזִי׃

records.literal_gloss: What to my beloved in my house, doing her the scheming the many? And flesh of holiness will pass from upon you, for your evil; then you exult.

en.L: What [right has] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} beloved in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house, when she has carried out [her] scheming, the many [schemes]? \q Can holy flesh take your evil away from you? \q Then you could exult.
en.B: What right does {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} beloved have in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house, when she has carried out so many evil schemes? \q Can sacred meat take your disaster away from you, \q so that you could rejoice?
en.R: My beloved people, what right do you have to come into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple? You have done so many evil things. \q Can the meat of your sacrifices keep disaster away from you, \q so that you can celebrate?

es.L: ¿Qué [derecho tiene] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} amada en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa, cuando ha llevado a cabo [sus] intrigas, las muchas [intrigas]? \q ¿Puede la carne santa quitar de ti tu maldad? \q Entonces podrías regocijarte.
es.B: ¿Qué derecho tiene {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} amada en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa, cuando ha llevado a cabo tantas intrigas malvadas? \q ¿Puede la carne de los sacrificios apartar de ti la desgracia, \q para que puedas alegrarte?
es.R: Pueblo amado, ¿qué derecho tienes de entrar en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} templo? Has hecho muchísimas maldades. \q ¿Puede la carne de tus sacrificios alejar de ti la desgracia, \q para que puedas celebrar?

fr.L: Qu’[a à faire] {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bien-aimée dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison, quand elle a exécuté [ses] intrigues, les nombreuses ? \q La viande sainte ôtera-t-elle de toi ton malheur ? \q Alors tu pourrais exulter.
fr.B: Quel droit {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bien-aimée a-t-elle dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison, après avoir mené à bien tant de mauvais desseins ? \q La viande consacrée peut-elle écarter de toi le malheur, \q pour que tu puisses te réjouir ?
fr.R: Mon peuple bien-aimé, de quel droit viens-tu dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} temple ? Tu as fait tant de mal. \q La viande de tes sacrifices peut-elle éloigner de toi le malheur, \q pour que tu puisses faire la fête ?

sw.L: Mpendwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ana [haki] gani katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, ameshatekeleza hila [zake], zile nyingi? \q Je, nyama takatifu itaweza kukuondolea uovu wako? \q Ndipo ungeweza kushangilia.
sw.B: Mpendwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ana haki gani katika nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, naye ametekeleza hila nyingi mbaya? \q Je, nyama ya sadaka inaweza kukuondolea maafa yako, \q ili upate kushangilia?
sw.R: Enyi watu wangu wapendwa, mna haki gani kuingia katika hekalu {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}? Mmetenda maovu mengi sana. \q Je, nyama ya dhabihu zenu inaweza kuyazuia maafa yasiwapate, \q ili mpate kusherehekea?

decisions.choice: the verse is read as a challenge: what right has Judah in God's house, and can sacrifices avert the disaster her sins have earned?
alternatives: for when you do evil, then you rejoice
the Greek: Can vows and holy meat take away your wickedness from you, or will you escape by these?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is very hard, and every reading of it is uncertain. "The many" does not fit the words around it, and "will pass from upon you" has no stated subject. The ancient Greek translation reads differently ("vows" where the Hebrew has "the many"), which suggests a different Hebrew text. The last line can also mean "for when you do evil, then you rejoice". All the readings agree on the main point: worship at the temple cannot cover the people's evil.

decisions.choice: my beloved: Judah, loved by God and pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: The word is a tender one (Psalm 127:2). Jeremiah 12:7 calls the people "the beloved of my soul". The words "she" and "you" in this verse are feminine: God speaks to Judah as to a wife in his house.

decisions.choice: holy flesh: the meat of sacrifices
decisions.reason: Part of many offerings was eaten at the temple as holy meat (Haggai 2:12). The people trusted their sacrifices to keep them safe, as they trusted the temple itself (7:4, 21-22).

decisions.choice: your evil: here, the disaster your evil brings
decisions.reason: The word means both evil done and the harm that follows it, a play the chapter uses (verses 11, 17). With "take away from you" the disaster is the more natural sense.

decisions.choice: verses 15-16 are poetry inside the prose sermon
decisions.reason: The sermon of verses 1-17 is prose, but here God's words take the form of a short poem in parallel lines, addressed to Judah as "you" (a woman). Verse 17 returns to prose.

decisions.choice: My beloved people ... my temple
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the people directly and says that God's house is the temple.

source.text: זַ֤יִת רַֽעֲנָן֙ יְפֵ֣ה פְרִי־תֹ֔אַר קָרָ֥א יְהוָ֖ה שְׁמֵ֑ךְ לְק֣וֹל׀הֲמוּלָּ֣ה גְדֹלָ֗ה הִצִּ֥ית אֵשׁ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ וְרָע֖וּ דָּלִיּוֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Olive tree luxuriant, beautiful of fruit [and] form, called Yahweh your name; to [the] sound of a roar great he has kindled fire on it, and are broken its branches.

en.L: A green olive tree, beautiful with fruit [and] form: \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called your name. \q At the sound of a great roar {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kindled fire on it, \q and its branches are broken.
en.B: 'A green olive tree, beautiful with fine fruit': \q that is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} named you. \q But with the noise of a great storm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set it on fire, \q and its branches will be broken.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} once called you a healthy olive tree, \q beautiful and full of good fruit. \q But now, with a noise like a mighty storm, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set it on fire, \q and its branches will be destroyed.

es.L: Olivo verde, hermoso en fruto [y] en forma: \q así llamó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu nombre. \q Al estruendo de un gran tumulto {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le ha prendido fuego, \q y sus ramas están quebradas.
es.B: “Olivo verde, hermoso y de buen fruto”: \q así te llamó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q Pero con el estruendo de una gran tormenta {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le prenderá fuego, \q y sus ramas quedarán quebradas.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te llamó una vez olivo frondoso, \q hermoso y lleno de buen fruto. \q Pero ahora, con un ruido como de gran tormenta, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le prenderá fuego, \q y sus ramas serán destruidas.

fr.L: Olivier verdoyant, beau de fruit [et] de forme : \q {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a appelé ton nom [ainsi]. \q Au bruit d’un grand fracas, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y a mis le feu, \q et ses branches sont brisées.
fr.B: “Olivier verdoyant, aux beaux fruits” : \q c’est le nom que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a donné. \q Mais dans le fracas d’une grande tempête, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y mettra le feu, \q et ses branches seront brisées.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’avait appelé un olivier plein de vie, \q beau et couvert de bons fruits. \q Mais maintenant, avec un bruit de grande tempête, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} va y mettre le feu, \q et ses branches seront détruites.

sw.L: Mzeituni mbichi, mzuri kwa matunda [na] umbo: \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliliita jina lako. \q Kwa sauti ya ngurumo kuu amewasha moto juu yake, \q na matawi yake yamevunjika.
sw.B: 'Mzeituni mbichi, mzuri wenye matunda mazuri': \q hilo ndilo jina {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alilokuita. \q Lakini kwa kelele za dhoruba kuu ataiwasha moto, \q na matawi yake yatavunjika.
sw.R: Zamani {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuita mzeituni wenye afya, \q mzuri na uliojaa matunda mazuri. \q Lakini sasa, kwa kelele kama za dhoruba kuu, ataiwasha moto, \q na matawi yake yataharibiwa.

decisions.choice: a green olive tree: God's people, planted and growing in his land
decisions.reason: The olive was among the most valued trees of Israel, rich in fruit and long-lived. God's people are pictured as an olive tree (Hosea 14:7; Psalm 52:10), and Paul uses the same picture (Romans 11:17-24).

decisions.choice: roar: a great tumult, like the noise of a storm or an army
decisions.reason: The word means a loud uproar; Ezekiel 1:24 compares a similar sound to the noise of an army. The fire may be pictured as lightning in a storm.

decisions.choice: he has kindled ... are broken: a coming judgment described as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for completed action, but the judgment is still to come (verse 17). Prophets often describe what God has decided as if it had already happened.

decisions.choice: are broken: shattered
decisions.reason: The verb can come from a root meaning "to break" or one meaning "to be bad". Beside the fire, broken or ruined branches suit the picture.

decisions.choice: he will set it on fire ... will be broken / destroyed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the verbs in the future, since the judgment is still to come (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks around the name
decisions.reason: The name God gave Judah is set in quotation marks; single marks, since the whole speech is already in double ones.

source.text: וַיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלַ֖יִךְ רָעָ֑ה בִּ֠גְלַל רָעַ֨ת בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם לְהַכְעִסֵ֖נִי לְקַטֵּ֥ר לַבָּֽעַל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh of hosts, the [one] planting you, has spoken against you disaster on account of [the] evil of [the] house of Israel and [the] house of Judah which they have done to themselves to provoke me by making smoke to the Baal.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you because of the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, which they have done to themselves, to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by making offerings smoke to Baal."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you because of the evil the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done to their own harm, provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger by burning offerings to Baal."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies planted you. But now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has announced that disaster will come on you. This is because of the evil things the people of Israel and Judah have done. They have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry by burning sacrifices to Baal, and they have only hurt themselves."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, que te plantó, ha pronunciado desgracia contra ti a causa de la maldad de la casa de Israel y de la casa de Judá, que han hecho para su propio mal, para provocar{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} quemando ofrendas a Baal».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, que te plantó, ha decretado la desgracia contra ti por la maldad que la casa de Israel y la casa de Judá han cometido para su propio daño, provocándo{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a ira con las ofrendas que queman a Baal».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos te plantó. Pero ahora {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha anunciado que vendrá la desgracia sobre ti. Es por las maldades que ha hecho el pueblo de Israel y de Judá. Ellos {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han hecho enojar quemando sacrificios a Baal, y solo se han hecho daño a sí mismos».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, qui t’a plantée, a prononcé le malheur contre toi, à cause de la méchanceté de la maison d’Israël et de la maison de Juda, qu’elles ont commise contre elles-mêmes, pour {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}offenser en faisant fumer des offrandes à Baal. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, qui t’a plantée, a décrété le malheur contre toi à cause du mal que la maison d’Israël et la maison de Juda ont fait à leur propre détriment, en {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}irritant par les offrandes qu’elles brûlent à Baal. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées t’a plantée. Mais maintenant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a annoncé que le malheur va venir sur toi. C’est à cause du mal qu’ont fait les gens d’Israël et de Juda. Ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont mis en colère en brûlant des sacrifices à Baal, et ils ne se sont fait du mal qu’à eux-mêmes. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, aliyekupanda, ametamka mabaya juu yako kwa sababu ya uovu wa nyumba ya Israeli na nyumba ya Yuda, waliojitendea wenyewe, ili kunikasirisha kwa kumfukizia Baali [sadaka]."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, aliyekupanda, ameamuru maafa juu yako kwa sababu ya uovu ambao nyumba ya Israeli na nyumba ya Yuda wameutenda kwa madhara yao wenyewe, wakinichokoza nikasirike kwa kumfukizia Baali sadaka."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ndiye aliyekupanda. Lakini sasa ametangaza kwamba maafa yatakujia. Hii ni kwa sababu ya mambo maovu waliyotenda watu wa Israeli na Yuda. Wamenikasirisha kwa kumtolea Baali dhabihu, nao wamejidhuru wao wenyewe tu."

decisions.choice: disaster ... evil: one word for both
decisions.reason: The same word means the evil the people have done and the disaster God declares against them. The punishment matches the sin.

decisions.choice: who planted you: God set his people in the land like a tree
decisions.reason: The verb picks up the olive tree of verse 16. God planted Israel as a choice vine (2:21; Psalm 80:9); the one who planted can also uproot (1:10).

decisions.choice: done to themselves, to provoke me: their worship harmed them and was meant to anger God
decisions.reason: "To themselves" can mean they did it to their own harm (7:19) or for their own purposes. The words "to provoke me" turn from God named in the third person to God speaking as "I": the speech is still his.

decisions.choice: provoke to anger: stir up God's anger by an offense
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy uses the verb for worship of other gods that angers the LORD (Deuteronomy 4:25; 31:29).

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts / the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: The book's fixed wording for this title, as in Isaiah (see Isaiah 1:9).

decisions.choice: planted you. But now he has announced
decisions.reason: Readable splits the verse into short sentences and supplies "but now" to mark the turn from planting to judgment.

decisions.choice: "desgracia ... maldad"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one word (ra'ah) for the disaster God sends and the evil the people did; Spanish needs two words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: mabaya ... uovu (Literal); maafa ... uovu (Balanced)
decisions.reason: One Hebrew word stands for the disaster and the evil (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps the shared root "-baya" / "-ovu" close, Balanced separates them as the sense requires.

decisions.choice: the closing » of the speech God began at 11:9
decisions.reason: French opened God's words to Jeremiah at 11:9 with « and closes them here, where the English closes its quotation.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֥ה הֽוֹדִיעַ֖נִי וָֽאֵדָ֑עָה אָ֖ז הִרְאִיתַ֥נִי מַעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh made known to me, and I knew; then you showed me their deeds.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made [it] known to me, and I knew; \q then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} showed me their deeds.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} let me know, and so I knew; \q then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} showed me what they were doing.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told me about their plot, and so I knew about it. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} showed me what they were doing.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [me lo] hizo saber, y lo supe; \q entonces {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me mostraste sus obras.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me lo dio a conocer, y así lo supe; \q entonces {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me mostraste lo que estaban haciendo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me habló de su complot, y así me enteré. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me mostraste lo que estaban haciendo.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me l’a fait connaître, et je l’ai su ; \q alors {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as montré leurs actions.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me l’a fait savoir, et je l’ai su ; \q alors {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as montré ce qu’ils faisaient.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a parlé de leur complot, et ainsi je l’ai su. \q {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as montré ce qu’ils faisaient.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akanijulisha, nami nikajua; \q ndipo {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ukanionyesha matendo yao.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alinijulisha, nami nikajua; \q ndipo ukanionyesha waliyokuwa wakiyafanya.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliniambia habari za njama yao, nami nikajua. \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulinionyesha walichokuwa wakifanya.

decisions.choice: the start of Jeremiah's first lament: his prayer to God about those who plot against him
decisions.reason: Verses 18-23 and 12:1-6 are the first of Jeremiah's prayers of complaint (also 15:10-21; 17:14-18; 18:18-23; 20:7-18). In them the prophet speaks to God about his own suffering, much as the psalms of lament do, and God answers.

decisions.choice: the LORD made known ... you showed me: Jeremiah turns from speaking about God to speaking to him
decisions.reason: The verse begins with God in the third person and ends addressing him as "you". This is common in prayer (Psalm 23:1-4).

decisions.choice: made it known: what God revealed is the plot described in verses 19 and 21
decisions.reason: The verse does not say what God made known; verse 19 tells it. The change from the sermon to Jeremiah's own story is sudden, and 12:6 tells of a plot within his own family.

decisions.choice: about their plot ... LORD, you
decisions.reason: Readable says what God made known and names the LORD as the one Jeremiah now speaks to, so the change of person is clear.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah speaks to God as "tú"
decisions.reason: This is the first of Jeremiah's laments, his own prayers to God about those who plot against him; as in the Psalms, he speaks to God as "tú", without "oh" before the name.

decisions.choice: first person, no quotation marks
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's first lament (11:18-12:6) is his own prayer and is set, like the oracles, without quotation marks; Swahili follows the turn from "BWANA" to "wewe" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: passé composé at every level in Jeremiah's lament (11:18-12:6)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's laments are prayers spoken to God, so they take the tenses of speech at every level, as the terms note sets.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֕י כְּכֶ֥בֶשׂ אַלּ֖וּף יוּבַ֣ל לִטְב֑וֹחַ וְלֹֽא־יָדַ֜עְתִּי כִּֽי־עָלַ֣י׀חָשְׁב֣וּ מַחֲשָׁב֗וֹת נַשְׁחִ֨יתָה עֵ֤ץ בְּלַחְמוֹ֙ וְנִכְרְתֶ֨נּוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֔ים וּשְׁמ֖וֹ לֹֽא־יִזָּכֵ֥ר עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: And I [was] like a lamb tame led to slaughter, and not I knew that against me they had devised devices: Let us destroy [the] tree with its bread, and let us cut him off from [the] land of [the] living, and his name not will be remembered again.

en.L: But I [was] like a tame lamb led to the slaughter, \q and I did not know that they had devised schemes against me: \q "Let us destroy the tree with its fruit, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, \q so that his name will be remembered no more."
en.B: I was like a trusting lamb being led away to be slaughtered; \q I did not know it was against me that they were making their plans: \q "Let us destroy the tree, fruit and all; let us cut him off from the land of the living, \q so that his name is never remembered again."
en.R: I had been like a gentle lamb being led away to be killed. \q I did not know they were making plans against me. \q They said, "Let us destroy the tree and its fruit. Let us kill him, \q so that no one will remember his name anymore."

es.L: Pero yo [era] como un cordero manso llevado al matadero, \q y no sabía que tramaban planes contra mí: \q «Destruyamos el árbol con su fruto, y cortémoslo de la tierra de los vivientes, \q y no se recuerde más su nombre».
es.B: Yo era como un cordero confiado que llevan al matadero; \q no sabía que era contra mí que hacían sus planes: \q «Destruyamos el árbol con todo y fruto; arranquémoslo de la tierra de los vivos, \q para que nunca más se recuerde su nombre».
es.R: Yo había sido como un cordero manso que llevan a matar. \q No sabía que estaban haciendo planes contra mí. \q Decían: «Destruyamos el árbol y su fruto. Matémoslo, \q para que nadie se acuerde más de su nombre».

fr.L: Et moi, [j’étais] comme un agneau docile qu’on mène à l’abattoir, \q et je ne savais pas qu’ils tramaient des projets contre moi : \q « Détruisons l’arbre avec son fruit, et retranchons-le de la terre des vivants, \q et qu’on ne se souvienne plus de son nom. »
fr.B: J’étais comme un agneau confiant qu’on emmène à l’abattoir ; \q je ne savais pas que c’était contre moi qu’ils formaient leurs plans : \q « Détruisons l’arbre avec son fruit ; retranchons-le de la terre des vivants, \q pour que son nom ne soit plus jamais rappelé. »
fr.R: J’étais comme un doux agneau qu’on emmène pour le tuer. \q Je ne savais pas qu’ils faisaient des plans contre moi. \q Ils disaient : « Détruisons l’arbre et son fruit. Tuons-le, \q pour que personne ne se souvienne plus de son nom. »

sw.L: Lakini mimi [nilikuwa] kama mwana-kondoo mpole anayepelekwa machinjoni, \q wala sikujua kwamba walikuwa wamefanya hila juu yangu: \q "Na tuuangamize mti pamoja na matunda yake, na tumkatilie mbali kutoka nchi ya walio hai, \q ili jina lake lisikumbukwe tena."
sw.B: Nilikuwa kama mwana-kondoo asiye na hila anayepelekwa kuchinjwa; \q sikujua kwamba ni juu yangu walikuwa wakipanga mipango yao: \q "Na tuuangamize mti pamoja na matunda yake; na tumkatilie mbali kutoka nchi ya walio hai, \q ili jina lake lisikumbukwe tena kamwe."
sw.R: Nilikuwa kama mwana-kondoo mpole anayepelekwa kuchinjwa. \q Sikujua kwamba walikuwa wakipanga njama dhidi yangu. \q Walisema, "Na tuuangamize mti pamoja na matunda yake. Na tumuue, \q ili hakuna mtu atakayelikumbuka jina lake tena."

decisions.choice: like a lamb led to the slaughter: one who goes unknowing and unresisting to his death
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:7 uses the same picture, with the same verb "led", of the servant who suffers in silence, and Isaiah 53:8 also speaks of being "cut off from the land of the living". The New Testament applies Isaiah's words to Jesus (Acts 8:32-33).

decisions.choice: tame: gentle and trusting, used to people
decisions.reason: The adjective describes a lamb raised close to people, which follows without suspicion. A related word means a close friend (Psalm 55:14). Jeremiah trusted those who were plotting against him (12:6).

decisions.choice: destroy the tree with its fruit: kill the man and put an end to all he produces
alternatives: destroy the tree in its sap (by a small change to the Hebrew)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "with its bread", a way of saying food or fruit. The fruit may be Jeremiah's words or the children he might have had (16:2). Some suggest a slight change of the letters to read "in its sap", meaning while it is still green; the meaning would be much the same.

decisions.choice: cut him off from the land of the living: kill him
decisions.reason: "The land of the living" is the world of those alive, set against the place of the dead (Psalm 27:13; Isaiah 53:8).

decisions.choice: his name will be remembered no more: no descendants, no memory
decisions.reason: A man's name lived on through his children and his reputation (Deuteronomy 25:6; Psalm 109:13). The plotters want Jeremiah wiped out completely.

decisions.choice: They said ... Let us kill him
decisions.reason: Readable introduces the plotters' words and gives the sense of "cut him off from the land of the living" (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: mwana-kondoo ... machinjoni
decisions.reason: "Mwana-kondoo" as the terms note sets it for Isaiah 53:7, the passage this line resembles (meaning decision m1).

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שֹׁפֵ֣ט צֶ֔דֶק בֹּחֵ֥ן כְּלָי֖וֹת וָלֵ֑ב אֶרְאֶ֤ה נִקְמָֽתְךָ֙ מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י אֵלֶ֖יךָ גִּלִּ֥יתִי אֶת־רִיבִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But Yahweh of hosts, judging righteousness, testing kidneys and heart, let me see your vengeance from them, for to you I have revealed my case.

en.L: But {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, judging righteously, \q testing kidneys and heart, \q let me see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} vengeance on them, \q for to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have revealed my case.
en.B: But {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who judge with justice, \q who test the inner feelings and the mind, \q let me see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take vengeance on them, \q for I have laid my case before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: But {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge fairly. \q You know what people think and feel deep inside. \q Let me see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pay them back for what they have done, \q because I have put my case in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands.

es.L: Pero {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, que juzgas con justicia, \q que pruebas los riñones y el corazón, \q vea yo {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} venganza sobre ellos, \q porque a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} he expuesto mi causa.
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} que juzgas con justicia, \q que examinas los sentimientos y la mente, \q déjame ver cómo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} te vengas de ellos, \q porque he puesto mi causa en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} juzgas con justicia. \q Sabes lo que la gente piensa y siente en lo más profundo. \q Déjame ver cómo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} les das su merecido, \q porque he puesto mi causa en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos.

fr.L: Mais {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, qui juges avec justice, \q qui sondes les reins et le cœur, \q que je voie {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vengeance sur eux, \q car c’est à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que j’ai exposé ma cause.
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui juges avec justice, \q qui éprouves les sentiments et les pensées, \q fais-moi voir {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vengeance sur eux, \q car c’est à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que j’ai confié ma cause.
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} juges de façon juste. \q Tu sais ce que les gens pensent et ressentent au fond d’eux-mêmes. \q Fais-moi voir comment {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} leur rendras ce qu’ils ont fait, \q car j’ai remis ma cause entre {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains.

sw.L: Lakini Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, unayehukumu kwa haki, \q unayejaribu figo na moyo, \q nione kisasi {{deity_pronoun:chako|Chako}} juu yao, \q kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} nimeifunua hoja yangu.
sw.B: Lakini Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unayehukumu kwa haki, \q unayeyajaribu mawazo ya ndani na moyo, \q nione ukilipiza kisasi juu yao, \q kwa maana nimeiweka hoja yangu mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.R: Lakini Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unahukumu kwa haki. \q Unajua watu wanayoyawaza na kuyahisi ndani kabisa. \q Nione ukiwalipa kwa yale waliyoyatenda, \q kwa sababu nimeiweka hoja yangu mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}.

decisions.choice: kidneys and heart: a person's inmost feelings and thoughts
decisions.reason: The kidneys were thought of as the seat of the deepest feelings, and the heart as the seat of thought and will. God alone tests them both (Psalm 7:10; Jeremiah 17:10). Jeremiah repeats this verse almost word for word in 20:12.

decisions.choice: vengeance: the just redress a judge gives a wronged person
decisions.reason: Jeremiah does not ask to take revenge himself. He brings his case to God as judge and asks to see God set things right (Deuteronomy 32:35; Psalm 94:1-2).

decisions.choice: I have revealed my case: I have laid my legal case open before you
alternatives: I have committed my case to you (by a different vowel, "rolled" it onto you)
decisions.reason: The verb means to uncover or reveal. With different vowels it would mean "rolled", as in "commit your way to the LORD" (Psalm 37:5). Either way Jeremiah leaves his case with God.

decisions.choice: judging righteously: who judges with justice
decisions.reason: The phrase describes the LORD as a judge who rules rightly; Jeremiah appeals to him as to a just court.

decisions.choice: you who judge ... you judge fairly
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "you" so that the titles of the LORD read as words spoken to him.

decisions.choice: LORD of hosts / LORD of Armies, addressed without "O"
decisions.reason: The divine name addressed directly has no "O", as in the Psalms and Isaiah.

decisions.choice: "los riñones y el corazón" (L); "los sentimientos y la mente" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the inmost self; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "les reins et le cœur"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture, which French readers know from older Bibles; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ עַל־אַנְשֵׁ֣י עֲנָת֔וֹת הַֽמְבַקְשִׁ֥ים אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א תִנָּבֵא֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תָמ֖וּת בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh concerning [the] men of Anathoth, the [ones] seeking your life, saying: Not you shall prophesy in [the] name of Yahweh, and not you will die by our hand,

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning the men of Anathoth, \q who seek your life, saying, \q "You shall not prophesy in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q so that you will not die by our hand,"
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this about the men of Anathoth, \q who are seeking your life and saying, \q "Do not prophesy in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q if you do not want to die at our hands,"
en.R: The men of Anathoth want to kill you. They say, \q "Stop prophesying in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, or we will kill you!" \q So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about them.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca de los hombres de Anatot, \q que buscan tu vida, diciendo: \q «No profetices en el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q para que no mueras a nuestras manos»,
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto acerca de los hombres de Anatot, \q que quieren quitarte la vida y te dicen: \q «No profetices en el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q si no quieres morir a nuestras manos»,
es.R: Los hombres de Anatot quieren matarte. Te dicen: \q «¡Deja de profetizar en el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, o te mataremos!». \q Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca de ellos.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au sujet des hommes d’Anatoth, \q qui en veulent à ta vie et disent : \q « Tu ne prophétiseras pas au nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q et tu ne mourras pas de notre main »,
fr.B: C’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci au sujet des hommes d’Anatoth, \q qui cherchent à t’ôter la vie et qui disent : \q « Ne prophétise pas au nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q si tu ne veux pas mourir de notre main »,
fr.R: Les hommes d’Anatoth veulent te tuer. Ils disent : \q « Arrête de prophétiser au nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, sinon nous te tuerons ! » \q Alors voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à leur sujet.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi kuhusu watu wa Anathothi, \q wanaoutafuta uhai wako, wakisema, \q "Usitabiri kwa jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q usije ukafa kwa mkono wetu,"
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo kuhusu watu wa Anathothi, \q wanaoutafuta uhai wako na kusema, \q "Usitabiri kwa jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q kama hutaki kufa mikononi mwetu,"
sw.R: Watu wa Anathothi wanataka kukuua. Wanasema, \q "Acha kutabiri kwa jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, la sivyo tutakuua!" \q Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema kuhusu wao.

decisions.choice: Anathoth: Jeremiah's hometown
decisions.reason: Anathoth was a town of priests in Benjamin, a few miles north of Jerusalem (Joshua 21:18), and Jeremiah came from a priestly family there (1:1). The plot against him comes from his own people (12:6).

decisions.choice: seek your life: try to kill you
decisions.reason: To seek someone's life is to want them dead (1 Kings 19:10).

decisions.choice: do not prophesy ... and you will not die: a threat; stop, or die
decisions.reason: The two clauses are joined by "and": if he stops prophesying, he will not die at their hands. It is a threat to silence him.

decisions.choice: therefore thus says the LORD: the sentence is broken off by the quotation and taken up again in verse 22
decisions.reason: The words "therefore thus says" are repeated at the start of verse 22, which gives the LORD's answer.

decisions.choice: The men of Anathoth want to kill you ... So this is what the LORD says about them.
decisions.reason: Readable tells first what the men of Anathoth are doing and then introduces the LORD's words, so the long broken sentence becomes three short ones. It also turns "you will die by our hand" into "we will kill you".

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י פֹקֵ֖ד עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם הַבַּֽחוּרִים֙ יָמֻ֣תוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב בְּנֵיהֶם֙ וּבְנ֣וֹתֵיהֶ֔ם יָמֻ֖תוּ בָּרָעָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts: Behold I [am] visiting on them; the young men will die by the sword, their sons and their daughters will die by the famine,

en.L: therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Look, I am about to punish them. \q The young men will die by the sword; \q their sons and their daughters will die by famine,
en.B: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: I am about to punish them. \q Their young men will die by the sword, \q and their sons and daughters will die by famine,
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: I am going to punish them. \q Their young men will be killed in war. \q Their sons and daughters will die of hunger.

es.L: por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: He aquí que los castigaré. \q Los jóvenes morirán a espada; \q sus hijos y sus hijas morirán de hambre,
es.B: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: Voy a castigarlos. \q Sus jóvenes morirán a espada, \q y sus hijos y sus hijas morirán de hambre,
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: Voy a castigarlos. \q Sus jóvenes morirán en la guerra. \q Sus hijos y sus hijas morirán de hambre.

fr.L: c’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Voici, je vais les punir. \q Les jeunes gens mourront par l’épée ; \q leurs fils et leurs filles mourront par la famine,
fr.B: {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Je vais les punir. \q Leurs jeunes gens mourront par l’épée, \q leurs fils et leurs filles mourront de famine,
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Je vais les punir. \q Leurs jeunes gens seront tués à la guerre. \q Leurs fils et leurs filles mourront de faim.

sw.L: kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Tazama, nitawaadhibu. \q Vijana watakufa kwa upanga; \q wana wao na binti zao watakufa kwa njaa,
sw.B: hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Karibu nitawaadhibu. \q Vijana wao watakufa kwa upanga, \q na wana wao na binti zao watakufa kwa njaa,
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Nitawaadhibu. \q Vijana wao watauawa vitani. \q Wana wao na binti zao watakufa kwa njaa.

decisions.choice: visit on: punish
decisions.reason: The verb means to attend to or look into something; with "on" it means to bring judgment on someone for what they have done (Exodus 20:5).

decisions.choice: young men: men in their prime, of an age to fight
decisions.reason: These are the town's young men, who would die in battle; the children would die of the famine that comes with war and siege.

decisions.choice: therefore thus says: takes up again the sentence begun in verse 21
decisions.reason: See verse 21.

decisions.choice: killed in war ... die of hunger
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for the sword and "hunger" for famine, as the book does elsewhere for this pair.

source.text: וּשְׁאֵרִ֕ית לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶ֖ה לָהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אָבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י עֲנָת֖וֹת שְׁנַ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And a remnant not will be to them, for I will bring disaster on [the] men of Anathoth, [the] year of their punishment.

en.L: and there will be no remnant for them, \q for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth, \q the year of their punishment.
en.B: and none of them will be left, \q for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth \q in the year of their punishment.
en.R: Not one of them will be left alive. \q I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth \q when the time comes to punish them.

es.L: y no les quedará remanente, \q porque traeré desgracia sobre los hombres de Anatot, \q el año de su castigo.
es.B: y no quedará ninguno de ellos, \q porque traeré la desgracia sobre los hombres de Anatot \q en el año de su castigo.
es.R: No quedará ninguno de ellos con vida. \q Traeré la desgracia sobre los hombres de Anatot \q cuando llegue el tiempo de castigarlos.

fr.L: et il ne leur restera pas de reste, \q car je ferai venir le malheur sur les hommes d’Anatoth, \q l’année de leur châtiment.
fr.B: et aucun d’eux ne survivra, \q car je ferai venir le malheur sur les hommes d’Anatoth \q l’année de leur châtiment.
fr.R: Pas un seul d’entre eux ne restera en vie. \q Je ferai venir le malheur sur les hommes d’Anatoth \q quand viendra le moment de les punir.

sw.L: wala hawatakuwa na mabaki, \q kwa maana nitaleta mabaya juu ya watu wa Anathothi, \q mwaka wa kuadhibiwa kwao.
sw.B: wala hakuna hata mmoja wao atakayebaki, \q kwa maana nitaleta maafa juu ya watu wa Anathothi \q katika mwaka wa kuadhibiwa kwao.
sw.R: Hakuna hata mmoja wao atakayebaki hai. \q Nitaleta maafa juu ya watu wa Anathothi \q wakati wa kuwaadhibu utakapofika.

decisions.choice: remnant: survivors, those left after a disaster
decisions.reason: No one of the plotters' families will survive. The judgment falls on them, not on the town for all time: men of Anathoth were among those who returned from exile (Ezra 2:23).

decisions.choice: the year of their punishment: the time set for their judgment
decisions.reason: The phrase recurs in Jeremiah (23:12; 48:44). It means the appointed time, not a particular calendar year.

decisions.choice: when the time comes to punish them
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "year" here, an appointed time (meaning decision m2).
